Generates the manuscript's tables and figures from the saved national
results. Each section is labelled with the manuscript item it produces.
Sections marked "not used in the manuscript" are additional figures kept
for reference.

| Manuscript item | Chunk | Output file in `figures/` |
|---|---|---|
| Figure 1 | `results_fig1_structure_revised` | `Fig01_woodland_structure.png` |
| Table 1 | `results_descriptives` | `Table1_descriptives.csv` |
| Figure 2a | `results_fig2a_threshold_sweep` | `Fig_dispersal_curve_national.png` |
| Figure 2b | `results_fig2b_threshold_ridgeline` | `Fig_dispersal_ridgeline_national.png` |
| Figure 3 | `results_fig3_named_cities_two_readings` | `Fig04d_two_readings_named_cities.png` |
| Figure 4 | `results_fig3_map` | `Fig03_connectivity_map.png` |
| Figures 5 and 6 | `sloss_publication_figures` | `Fig05_area_vs_fragmentation.png`, `Fig06_matched_pairs.png` |
| Figure 7 | `results_fig7_spacing_partial_plot` | `Fig_SLOSS_spacing_partial_effect.png` |
| Supplementary Table 1 | `city_set_and_constituents` | `TableS1_city_constituents.csv` |
| Supplementary Figure 1 and Table 2 | `sloss_publication_figures` | `Fig07_effect_across_city_size.png`, `Supp_woodland_amount_band_effects.csv` |
| Supplementary Table 3 | `results_supp_table2_top_patch_regions` | `TableS_spacing_top_patch_count_regions.csv` |
| Supplementary Table 4 | `results_supp_table4_city_connectivity` | `SuppTable4_city_connectivity.csv` |

Table 2, Supplementary Table 5 and Supplementary Figure 2 are produced in
`03_National_ECS.Rmd`.

# Setup

```{r setup}
source(here::here("scripts", "00_setup.R"))
# patchwork is used by several figure chunks below. Loading it once here
# means the chunks do not depend on the order they are run in.
library(patchwork)
```

Loads the named urban regions and the clipped NFI woodland polygons saved by `01b`.

```{r load_checkpoints}
library(sf)

urban_regions_named <- readRDS(
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "07b_urban_regions_named.rds")
)

nfi_urban <- readRDS(
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "nfi_urban_regions.rds")
)

cat("urban_regions_named:", nrow(urban_regions_named), "regions\n")
```

# Named-region data prep (needed for the delineation figure below)

```{r prepare_bua_data}
# Filter to England using the LSOA-to-Region lookup rather than the
# census population table. LSOAs cover the whole country without gaps,
# whereas the census table's BUA22 codes do not match for central London,
# so a semi_join against it would drop inner London from `bua`.
england_buas <- lsoa_lookup |>
  filter(startsWith(RGN22CD, "E12")) |>
  distinct(BUA22CD)

bua <- bua |>
  semi_join(england_buas, by = "BUA22CD")

# Add population counts and names. A left_join keeps any BUA missing from
# the census population table, with population = NA.
bua <- bua |>
  left_join(
    census |>
      dplyr::select(
        BUA22CD = `BUA code`,
        population = Counts,
        size_classification = `BUA size classification`
      ),
    by = "BUA22CD"
  )
```

# Results data prep

Loads the national results, keeps the regions that were modelled successfully, and defines the figure-saving helper and the size-adjustment model used by the figures below.

```{r fit_residual_models}
library(ggplot2)
if (!requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggrepel", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(ggrepel)

# Figures are written here as well as shown in the plot pane. The folder
# is in the project, not on the checkpoint drive, because these are small
# outputs that belong with the manuscript.
figures_dir <- here::here("figures")
dir.create(figures_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

save_fig <- function(plot_obj, name, width = 9, height = 6.5) {
  ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, paste0(name, ".png")),
         plot_obj, width = width, height = height, dpi = 300)
  invisible(plot_obj)
}

# Defined here as well as in the national_loop chunk of
# 03_National_ECS.Rmd, so the analysis and figure chunks below can be run
# without re-running the national build.
results_path <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "08_national_ecs_results.csv")

results <- read.csv(results_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ok <- results |> filter(is.na(error), total_area_ha > 0)
ok$log_area <- log(ok$total_area_ha)

fit_residuals <- function(pct_col) {
  sub <- ok |> filter(!is.na(.data[[pct_col]]))
  fit <- lm(reformulate("log_area", response = pct_col), data = sub)
  sub$predicted <- predict(fit)
  sub$residual <- sub[[pct_col]] - sub$predicted
  list(data = sub, fit = fit)
}

res_59 <- fit_residuals("ECS_pct_59")
res_99 <- fit_residuals("ECS_pct_99")
res_512 <- fit_residuals("ECS_pct_512")

cat("ECS_pct_59 model R-squared:", round(summary(res_59$fit)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
cat("ECS_pct_99 model R-squared:", round(summary(res_99$fit)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
cat("ECS_pct_512 model R-squared:", round(summary(res_512$fit)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
```

# Figure 1: extent and patch structure

Plots the distribution of woodland cover and of area-weighted patch size across regions. It needs `10_patch_size_distribution.csv` from `03b`.

```{r results_fig1_structure_revised}
patch_path <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "10_patch_size_distribution.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(patch_path))

ps <- read.csv(patch_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |> filter(is.na(error))

# The patch-size pass processes regions in the same smallest-first order
# as the national run, so a partial file is biased towards small regions.
# Warn rather than report a skewed distribution.
is_partial <- nrow(ps) < nrow(ok)
if (is_partial) {
  warning("Patch-size file is incomplete (", nrow(ps), " of ", nrow(ok),
          " regions). Figure 1 is PRELIMINARY and biased towards small regions.")
}

fig1_dat <- ok |>
  mutate(woodland_pct = 100 * total_area_ha / area_ha) |>
  inner_join(ps |> dplyr::select(region, awm_patch_ha, largest_patch_ha, mean_patch_ha),
             by = "region")

p1a <- ggplot(fig1_dat, aes(x = woodland_pct)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey45", colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(fig1_dat$woodland_pct), colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = median(fig1_dat$woodland_pct), y = Inf, vjust = 1.8, hjust = -0.12,
           label = sprintf("median %.1f%%", median(fig1_dat$woodland_pct)),
           colour = "firebrick", fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  labs(x = "Woodland cover (% of region area)", y = "Number of regions") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold"))

med_awm <- median(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha)
p1b <- ggplot(fig1_dat, aes(x = awm_patch_ha)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue4", colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med_awm, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = med_awm, y = Inf, vjust = 1.8, hjust = -0.12,
           label = sprintf("median %.2f ha", med_awm),
           colour = "firebrick", fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  # The y-axis label is repeated on both panels so it is clear that the
  # bars count regions; without it, the x-axis (a within-region statistic)
  # can be misread as showing patches or a single region.
  labs(x = "Typical patch size within a region (ha, log scale)",
       y = "Number of regions") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))

# The figure describes regions, not woodland in aggregate: the pooled
# national figure differs substantially from the region-wise median, so a
# statement about "England's urban woodland" would be a different claim
# from one about the typical urban area. Each region contributes one
# observation to each panel, and bars count regions. Panel (b) is
# area-weighted within each region, so it is not dragged down by large
# numbers of tiny fragments: it reports the patch size that a typical
# hectare of the region's woodland sits in.
fig1 <- (p1a | p1b) +
  plot_annotation(
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
                  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.15)))
print(fig1)
save_fig(fig1, "Fig01_woodland_structure", width = 11.5, height = 5.4)

cat("\n--- Panel (b) summary ---\n")
cat(sprintf("  area-weighted mean patch size: median %.3f ha (IQR %.3f-%.3f, max %.1f)\n",
            median(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha), quantile(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha, .25),
            quantile(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha, .75), max(fig1_dat$awm_patch_ha)))
cat(sprintf("  count-based mean for comparison: median %.3f ha\n", median(fig1_dat$mean_patch_ha)))
cat(sprintf("  largest patch per region: median %.2f ha, max %.1f ha\n",
            median(fig1_dat$largest_patch_ha), max(fig1_dat$largest_patch_ha)))
cat(sprintf("  regions containing at least one patch >= 1 ha:  %.1f%%\n",
            100 * mean(fig1_dat$largest_patch_ha >= 1)))
cat(sprintf("  regions containing at least one patch >= 10 ha: %.1f%%\n",
            100 * mean(fig1_dat$largest_patch_ha >= 10)))
```

# Table 1: descriptive statistics

Calculates the descriptive statistics quoted in the Results and writes Table 1 as a CSV.

```{r results_descriptives}
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)

desc <- ok |>
  mutate(woodland_pct = 100 * total_area_ha / area_ha,
         mean_patch_ha = total_area_ha / n_patches)

# Join the patch-size distribution, which supplies the area-weighted mean
# patch size. The count-based mean above treats a 0.05 ha scrap and a
# 40 ha wood as equal observations and understates the patch size
# experienced by woodland; the area-weighted version is ECS evaluated at
# a threshold of zero, and is the figure reported.
patch_path <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "10_patch_size_distribution.csv")
if (file.exists(patch_path)) {
  ps_all <- read.csv(patch_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |> filter(is.na(error))
  desc <- desc |> left_join(ps_all |> dplyr::select(region, awm_patch_ha, largest_patch_ha),
                            by = "region")
  if (nrow(ps_all) < nrow(ok)) {
    warning("Patch-size file incomplete (", nrow(ps_all), " of ", nrow(ok),
            " regions) -- area-weighted figures are PRELIMINARY.", call. = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  desc$awm_patch_ha <- NA_real_; desc$largest_patch_ha <- NA_real_
  warning("10_patch_size_distribution.csv not found; area-weighted patch size unavailable.",
          call. = FALSE)
}

qr <- function(x) sprintf("median %.3f (IQR %.3f-%.3f, max %.2f)",
                          median(x, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(x, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
                          quantile(x, .75, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE))

cat("Regions modelled:", nrow(desc), "\n")
cat("Total urban area:", format(round(sum(desc$area_ha)), big.mark = ","), "ha\n")
cat("Total urban woodland:", format(round(sum(desc$total_area_ha)), big.mark = ","), "ha\n")
cat("Woodland as % of urban land:", round(100 * sum(desc$total_area_ha) / sum(desc$area_ha), 2), "%\n\n")
cat("Woodland cover (%):      ", qr(desc$woodland_pct), "\n")
cat("Patches per region:      ", qr(desc$n_patches), "\n")
cat("Mean patch size (ha):    ", qr(desc$mean_patch_ha), "\n")
cat("  regions with mean patch < 1 ha:  ", round(100 * mean(desc$mean_patch_ha < 1), 1), "%\n")
cat("  regions with mean patch < 0.5 ha:", round(100 * mean(desc$mean_patch_ha < 0.5), 1), "%\n\n")

for (th in c(59, 99, 512)) {
  v <- desc[[paste0("ECS_pct_", th)]]
  cat(sprintf("%3dm: median %.3f | mean %.3f | %%>=50%% connected: %.1f%%\n",
              th, median(v, na.rm = TRUE), mean(v, na.rm = TRUE),
              100 * mean(v >= 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)))
}

# Regions with relative ECS of at least 0.5 at 512 m but not at 59 m
# (quoted in the Results).
both <- desc |> filter(!is.na(ECS_pct_59), !is.na(ECS_pct_512))
sorted_n <- sum(both$ECS_pct_512 >= 0.5 & both$ECS_pct_59 < 0.5)
cat(sprintf("\nConnected for a 512m disperser but NOT a 59m disperser: %d of %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            sorted_n, nrow(both), 100 * sorted_n / nrow(both)))

# Table 1, formatted for the manuscript
# Reported as median / IQR / range rather than mean +- SD, because every
# variable here is strongly right-skewed and a mean would misrepresent
# the typical region.
fmt <- function(x, dp = 2, big = FALSE) {
  f <- function(v) if (big) format(round(v, dp), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE) else sprintf(paste0("%.", dp, "f"), v)
  c(median = f(median(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    iqr    = paste0(f(quantile(x, .25, na.rm = TRUE)), "–", f(quantile(x, .75, na.rm = TRUE))),
    range  = paste0(f(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)), "–", f(max(x, na.rm = TRUE))))
}

# Rows are grouped under subheadings because they are in different units
# (percentages, hectares, counts) and are not meant to be compared with
# one another. The table is a reference of exact values; comparisons
# between the three movement thresholds are made in Figure 2, where they
# share a common scale.
vars <- list(
  "__EXTENT" = NULL,
  "Woodland cover (% of region area)"        = fmt(desc$woodland_pct, 2),
  "Total woodland per region (ha)"           = fmt(desc$total_area_ha, 2, big = TRUE),
  "__STRUCTURE" = NULL,
  "Woodland patches per region"              = fmt(desc$n_patches, 0, big = TRUE),
  "Typical patch size, area-weighted (ha)"   = fmt(desc$awm_patch_ha, 3),
  "Largest patch in region (ha)"             = fmt(desc$largest_patch_ha, 2),
  "__CONNECTIVITY" = NULL,
  "Woodland accessible at 59 m (%)"          = fmt(100 * desc$ECS_pct_59, 1),
  "Woodland accessible at 99 m (%)"          = fmt(100 * desc$ECS_pct_99, 1),
  "Woodland accessible at 512 m (%)"         = fmt(100 * desc$ECS_pct_512, 1)
)

group_labels <- c("__EXTENT" = "Extent", "__STRUCTURE" = "Structure",
                  "__CONNECTIVITY" = "Connectivity")

grab <- function(v, field) if (is.null(v)) "" else unname(v[[field]])

tab1 <- tibble::tibble(
  Variable = ifelse(names(vars) %in% names(group_labels),
                    unname(group_labels[names(vars)]), names(vars)),
  Median   = vapply(vars, grab, character(1), "median"),
  IQR      = vapply(vars, grab, character(1), "iqr"),
  Range    = vapply(vars, grab, character(1), "range")
)

cat("\n--- Table 1 ---\n")
print(as.data.frame(tab1), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nn =", nrow(desc), "urban regions\n")

# A file can be briefly locked by a file-sync client or by being open in
# Excel. Do not let that abort the chunk; the table is printed above
# regardless.
tryCatch(
  write.csv(tab1, file.path(figures_dir, "Table1_descriptives.csv"), row.names = FALSE),
  error = function(e) warning("Could not write Table1_descriptives.csv (file locked?): ",
                              conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE)
)
```

# Figures 2a and 2b: connectivity across movement thresholds

Both panels use the national movement-threshold sweep (relative ECS for
every region at every 10 m from 0 to 1,000 m), computed in the
`threshold_sweep_loop` and `threshold_sweep_extend_loop` chunks of
`03_National_ECS.Rmd`. The plotting code is the same as in the
`plot_threshold_sweep` and `plot_threshold_ridgeline` chunks there. The
three percentages marked on Figure 2a are calculated from the results.

```{r results_fig2a_threshold_sweep}
prior_sweep <- read.csv(file.path(checkpoint_dir, "08_national_ecs_threshold_sweep.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

sweep_summary <- prior_sweep |>
  filter(!is.na(ECS_pct)) |>
  group_by(threshold_m) |>
  summarise(
    median_pct = median(ECS_pct),
    q25 = quantile(ECS_pct, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(ECS_pct, 0.75),
    pct_above_50 = 100 * mean(ECS_pct >= 0.5),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Share of regions with relative ECS >= 0.5 at the three focal thresholds,
# calculated from the national results.
marker_thresholds <- data.frame(
  threshold_m = c(59, 99, 512),
  label = c("59m", "99m", "512m"),
  pct = round(100 * c(mean(ok$ECS_pct_59 >= 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
                      mean(ok$ECS_pct_99 >= 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
                      mean(ok$ECS_pct_512 >= 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)), 1)
)

fig_dispersal_curve <- ggplot(sweep_summary, aes(x = threshold_m, y = pct_above_50)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = marker_thresholds, aes(x = threshold_m, y = pct), colour = "grey20", size = 2.5) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = marker_thresholds, aes(x = threshold_m, y = pct, label = paste0(label, ": ", pct, "%")),
                             colour = "grey20", size = 3.3, label.size = 0, fill = alpha("white", 0.85),
                             min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.6, seed = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1000, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Movement threshold (m)",
    y = "Regions functioning as a connected network (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.2))
print(fig_dispersal_curve)
save_fig(fig_dispersal_curve, "Fig_dispersal_curve_national", width = 10, height = 7)

tryCatch(
  write.csv(sweep_summary, file.path(figures_dir, "TableS_dispersal_curve_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE),
  error = function(e) warning("Could not write TableS_dispersal_curve_summary: ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE)
)
```

The sweep only has rows at multiples of 10 m, so 59 m and 99 m are
shown by their nearest sweep values, 60 m and 100 m.

```{r results_fig2b_threshold_ridgeline}
if (!requireNamespace("ggridges", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggridges", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(ggridges)

selected_thresholds <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1000, by = 100), 60, 512)))
ridge_dat <- prior_sweep |> filter(!is.na(ECS_pct), threshold_m %in% selected_thresholds)
ridge_dat$threshold_label <- factor(paste0(ridge_dat$threshold_m, "m"),
                                     levels = paste0(rev(selected_thresholds), "m"))

fig_dispersal_ridgeline <- ggplot(ridge_dat, aes(x = ECS_pct, y = threshold_label, fill = after_stat(x))) +
  geom_density_ridges_gradient(scale = 2.2, rel_min_height = 0.01, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Connectivity", labels = scales::percent, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Expected Cluster Size (%)",
    y = "Movement threshold"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.2))
print(fig_dispersal_ridgeline)
save_fig(fig_dispersal_ridgeline, "Fig_dispersal_ridgeline_national", width = 10, height = 8.5)
```

# Figure 4: geography of connectivity

```{r results_fig3_map}
# Fill is the percentile rank of ECS_pct_59, not the raw value. Most
# regions sit in a narrow band, so a linear scale would spend most of the
# viridis gradient on a range almost nothing occupies and show only
# extreme outliers (for example Milton Keynes). Percentile rank spends
# the full colour range on the actual distribution, whatever its shape.
map_conn <- urban_regions_named |>
  inner_join(desc |> dplyr::select(region, ECS_pct_59, ECS_pct_99),
             by = c("bua_name" = "region")) |>
  mutate(pct_rank_59 = dplyr::percent_rank(ECS_pct_59))

fig_map <- ggplot(map_conn) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_rank_59), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", labels = scales::percent,
                       name = "Connectivity\npercentile\n(59 m)") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "right")
print(fig_map)
save_fig(fig_map, "Fig03_connectivity_map", width = 9, height = 11)
```

# City set (Supplementary Table 1; also used by Figure 3 and Supplementary Table 4)

Selects the regions that contain an ONS Major Town or City, and writes Supplementary Table 1 listing the designated places merged into each region.

```{r city_set_and_constituents}
library(sf)
# dplyr is attached explicitly: if this chunk is run in a fresh session
# without `setup`, filter() resolves to stats::filter() and fails on an
# sf tibble. Attaching dplyr here puts it ahead of stats on the search
# path.
library(dplyr)

tc <- readRDS(file.path(checkpoint_dir, "major_towns_cities.rds")) |> st_make_valid()
tc$tcity_area <- as.numeric(st_area(tc))

urb_valid <- st_make_valid(urban_regions_named)
geoms <- urb_valid |> filter(bua_name %in% ok$region)

inter <- suppressWarnings(
  st_intersection(geoms |> dplyr::select(bua_name), tc |> dplyr::select(TCITY15NM, tcity_area)))
inter$overlap <- as.numeric(st_area(inter))

city_match <- st_drop_geometry(inter) |>
  group_by(TCITY15NM) |>
  slice_max(overlap, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(coverage = overlap / tcity_area) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(coverage >= 0.3)

city_regions <- sort(unique(city_match$bua_name))
cat("designated cities matched:", nrow(city_match), "of", nrow(tc), "\n")
cat("distinct urban regions in the city set:", length(city_regions), "\n")
cat("regions absorbing more than one designated city:",
    sum(table(city_match$bua_name) > 1), "\n\n")

# Supplementary Table 1: the designated places merged into each region.
constituents <- city_match |>
  group_by(Region = bua_name) |>
  summarise(`Designated cities within region` = paste(sort(TCITY15NM), collapse = ", "),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(ok |> dplyr::select(region, area_ha), by = c("Region" = "region")) |>
  mutate(`Region area (ha)` = format(round(area_ha), big.mark = ",")) |>
  dplyr::select(Region, `Designated cities within region`, n, `Region area (ha)`) |>
  arrange(desc(n), Region)

cat("--- regions containing more than one designated city ---\n")
print(as.data.frame(constituents |> filter(n > 1) |> dplyr::select(-`Region area (ha)`)),
      row.names = FALSE)

tryCatch({
  write.csv(constituents, file.path(figures_dir, "TableS1_city_constituents.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  library(officer)
  read_docx() |>
    body_add_par(paste0(
      "Table S1. Urban regions used for between-city comparison, and the ONS-designated ",
      "Major Towns and Cities each contains. Regions are delineated by continuity of built-up ",
      "land, so several absorb more than one designated city; connectivity values reported ",
      "against a region name describe the whole conurbation."), style = "Table Caption") |>
    body_add_table(as.data.frame(constituents), style = "Table Professional", first_row = TRUE) |>
    print(target = file.path(figures_dir, "TableS1_city_constituents.docx"))
  cat("\nWrote TableS1_city_constituents.csv and .docx\n")
}, error = function(e) warning("Could not write Table S1: ", conditionMessage(e), call. = FALSE))
```

# Figure 3: named cities, two readings of connectivity

Reuses `ok` and `city_regions` from the city-set chunk above. Variable
names carry a `_fig3` suffix so they do not overwrite the `cities`
object used by the city figures below, and each panel has its own x-axis
label.

```{r results_fig3_named_cities_two_readings}
library(mgcv)

build_leaderboard_fig3 <- function(pct_col, floor_ha = 10) {
  sub <- ok |> filter(total_area_ha >= floor_ha, area_ha > 0, !is.na(.data[[pct_col]]))
  sub$log_area_region <- log(sub$area_ha)
  sub$log_woodland <- log(sub$total_area_ha)
  m <- gam(reformulate(c("s(log_area_region, k = 5)", "s(log_woodland, k = 5)"), response = pct_col),
           data = sub, family = betar(link = "logit"), method = "REML")
  sub$expected_pct <- predict(m, type = "response")
  sub$divergence_pp <- 100 * (sub[[pct_col]] - sub$expected_pct)
  sub
}
lb_59_fig3 <- build_leaderboard_fig3("ECS_pct_59")

cities_fig3 <- ok |> filter(region %in% city_regions, area_ha > 0, !is.na(ECS_pct_59)) |>
  left_join(lb_59_fig3 |> dplyr::select(region, expected_pct, divergence_pp), by = "region")

cat("=== Divergence_pp for the named-places cities ===\n")
print(cities_fig3 |> filter(region %in% c("Milton Keynes", "Manchester & Bolton (Bolton)", "London",
                                           "Gloucester")) |>
        transmute(region, ECS_ha_59, ECS_pct_59, expected_pct, divergence_pp))

top_n_city <- 8

# Each panel is its own leaderboard: the eight cities with the highest value of
# that measure, sorted within the panel.
make_leaderboard_panel_fig3 <- function(value_col, axis_label, scale = 1) {
  d <- cities_fig3 |>
    arrange(desc(.data[[value_col]])) |>
    transmute(region, value = scale * .data[[value_col]]) |>
    slice_head(n = top_n_city) |>
    arrange(value)
  d$region <- factor(d$region, levels = d$region)
  ggplot(d, aes(x = value, y = region)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue4", width = 0.6) +
    labs(x = axis_label, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10.5)
}

p_ecs_ha  <- make_leaderboard_panel_fig3("ECS_ha_59", "Raw ECS (ha)")
p_ecs_pct <- make_leaderboard_panel_fig3("ECS_pct_59", "Relative ECS (% of the region's woodland)", scale = 100)

fig_named_cities <- p_ecs_ha | p_ecs_pct
print(fig_named_cities)
save_fig(fig_named_cities, "Fig04d_two_readings_named_cities", width = 9.5, height = 5.5)
```

# Figures 5 and 6 and Supplementary Figure 1: woodland amount against fragmentation

Fits the beta-family GAMs and the matched-pairs comparison behind Figures 5 and 6, and the woodland-band analysis behind Supplementary Figure 1. Writes the three figures and the band estimates (Supplementary Table 2).

```{r sloss_publication_figures}
if (!requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("patchwork", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(patchwork)

# 10 ha floor: below this, ECS_pct is dominated by a handful of tiny
# slivers and behaves as noise rather than a meaningful connectivity
# measure (the same rationale as the minimum-area floors used elsewhere).
sl <- ok |>
  filter(total_area_ha >= 10, !is.na(ECS_pct_59), n_patches > 0)

# Figure 5: woodland amount against fragmentation, same data, same y-axis
# Both panels are single-predictor models so that the deviance-explained
# values are a like-for-like comparison. The two-predictor model (area
# and fragmentation together) is in Table 2 (`results_table2_model_comparison`
# in 03_National_ECS.Rmd).
#
# Panel (b) uses n_patches rather than nClusters. nClusters is the count
# of clusters produced by thresholding the graph at 59 m, and ECS is
# computed from the same clusters' areas (sum(cluster_area^2) /
# total_area), so regressing one on the other is partly circular.
# n_patches is the count of physical woodland patches identified from the
# raster before any threshold is applied, so it is independent of the ECS
# calculation.
#
# Model class: ECS_pct_59 is a bounded proportion (0 to 1), for which OLS
# has the wrong distributional assumption (heteroscedastic near the
# boundaries) and the wrong functional form (an OLS fit on log(n_patches)
# predicts negative connectivity at high patch counts). The models are
# therefore beta-family GAMs (logit link, mgcv::betar) with k = 5, which
# allows one real bend without chasing noise in the sparse tails. R^2 is
# replaced by deviance explained, the equivalent summary for this model
# class.
library(mgcv)

m_area <- gam(ECS_pct_59 ~ s(log(total_area_ha), k = 5), data = sl, family = betar(link = "logit"))
m_frag <- gam(ECS_pct_59 ~ s(log(n_patches), k = 5), data = sl, family = betar(link = "logit"))
dev_area <- summary(m_area)$dev.expl
dev_frag <- summary(m_frag)$dev.expl

pa <- ggplot(sl, aes(x = total_area_ha, y = ECS_pct_59)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.22, colour = "grey35", size = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 5),
              method.args = list(family = betar(link = "logit")),
              colour = "steelblue", fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  annotate("label", x = min(sl$total_area_ha), y = 0.97, hjust = 0, label.size = 0,
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, size = 4.2, fontface = "bold",
           label = sprintf("Deviance explained = %.0f%%", 100 * dev_area)) +
  labs(x = "Total woodland area (ha, log scale)",
       y = "Expected Cluster Size (%)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))

pb <- ggplot(sl, aes(x = n_patches, y = ECS_pct_59)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.22, colour = "grey35", size = 1.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 5),
              method.args = list(family = betar(link = "logit")),
              colour = "firebrick", fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  annotate("label", x = max(sl$n_patches), y = 0.97, hjust = 1, label.size = 0,
           fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, size = 4.2, fontface = "bold",
           label = sprintf("Deviance explained = %.0f%%", 100 * dev_frag)) +
  labs(x = "Number of separate woodland patches (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        axis.text.y = element_blank())

fig1 <- (pa | pb) +
  plot_annotation(
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
  )
print(fig1)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "Fig05_area_vs_fragmentation.png"), fig1,
       width = 11, height = 5.6, dpi = 300)
cat("Fig 1 -- deviance explained, area:", round(dev_area, 3), "| fragmentation:", round(dev_frag, 3), "\n")

# Figure 6: matched pairs (systematic nearest-area search)
# Uses n_patches rather than nClusters_59: nClusters is a property of the
# same thresholded graph that ECS is computed from, so comparing outcomes
# by cluster count is partly circular. n_patches is independent of the
# ECS calculation.
n <- nrow(sl); area <- sl$total_area_ha; pct <- sl$ECS_pct_59
region <- sl$region; nc <- sl$n_patches

best_j <- integer(n); rel_j <- numeric(n)
for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  rel <- abs(area - area[i]) / area[i]; rel[i] <- Inf
  j <- which.min(rel); best_j[i] <- j; rel_j[i] <- rel[j]
}

pairs_fig <- data.frame(
  region_a = region, area_a = area, nc_a = nc, ecs_a = pct,
  region_b = region[best_j], area_b = area[best_j], nc_b = nc[best_j], ecs_b = pct[best_j],
  rel_diff = rel_j
) |>
  filter(rel_diff <= 0.05) |>
  mutate(outcome_diff = abs(ecs_a - ecs_b),
         key = paste(pmin(region_a, region_b), pmax(region_a, region_b))) |>
  distinct(key, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(rel_diff, key)

# One row per region: a region that is the nearest-area match for several
# others would otherwise recur across rows, which reads as padding rather
# than independent evidence.
#
# Pairs are sorted by rel_diff (closest area match first), not by the
# outcome difference, before conflicts are resolved. When a region is the
# nearest-area match for several others, whichever candidate pair is
# processed first claims it; sorting by the outcome difference would let
# the pair with the largest connectivity gap always win, enriching the
# sample for bigger apparent effects. Sorting by area-match closeness
# makes the rule independent of the outcome being tested.
used <- character(0); keep <- logical(nrow(pairs_fig))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairs_fig))) {
  if (!(pairs_fig$region_a[i] %in% used) && !(pairs_fig$region_b[i] %in% used)) {
    keep[i] <- TRUE
    used <- c(used, pairs_fig$region_a[i], pairs_fig$region_b[i])
  }
}
# The full set is kept separately, not just the pairs shown in the figure:
# the SLOSS research agenda (Fahrig et al.) recommends comparing multiple
# matched landscapes rather than a few illustrative ones, and the summary
# chunk below reports across all of them.
#
# pairs_fig_full is the formal sample, built from woodland-area
# similarity only, with no knowledge of ECS. Sorting by outcome_diff
# happens only when choosing the pairs to display, never when deciding
# which pairs survive the de-duplication above.
pairs_fig_full <- pairs_fig[keep, ]
# Display set: the seven largest differences among pairs in which the region
# with fewer patches was the better connected. The statistical tests above use
# every pair, including those that go the other way.
pairs_fig <- pairs_fig_full |>
  filter((nc_a < nc_b & ecs_a > ecs_b) | (nc_b < nc_a & ecs_b > ecs_a)) |>
  arrange(desc(outcome_diff)) |>
  head(7)

pl <- pairs_fig |>
  mutate(
    win_region  = ifelse(ecs_a >= ecs_b, region_a, region_b),
    win_ecs     = pmax(ecs_a, ecs_b),
    win_nc      = ifelse(ecs_a >= ecs_b, nc_a, nc_b),
    lose_region = ifelse(ecs_a >= ecs_b, region_b, region_a),
    lose_ecs    = pmin(ecs_a, ecs_b),
    lose_nc     = ifelse(ecs_a >= ecs_b, nc_b, nc_a),
    pair_label  = sprintf("%s  vs  %s\n(~%.0f ha each)", win_region, lose_region, area_a)
  ) |>
  arrange(win_ecs - lose_ecs) |>
  mutate(pair_label = factor(pair_label, levels = pair_label))

fig2 <- ggplot(pl) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = pair_label, yend = pair_label, x = lose_ecs, xend = win_ecs),
               colour = "grey65", linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pair_label, x = lose_ecs), colour = "firebrick", size = 5.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pair_label, x = win_ecs), colour = "forestgreen", size = 5.5) +
  geom_text(aes(y = pair_label, x = lose_ecs, label = lose_nc), colour = "white", size = 2.7, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(aes(y = pair_label, x = win_ecs, label = win_nc), colour = "white", size = 2.7, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(-0.02, 1.05)) +
  labs(
    x = "Expected Cluster Size (%)", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, lineheight = 1.15),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.1),
        plot.margin = margin(12, 18, 12, 12))
print(fig2)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "Fig06_matched_pairs.png"), fig2, width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 300)

# Supplementary Figure 1: the effect across woodland amount bands, at both thresholds
# Model class: each band's effect is estimated with a beta-family GLM
# (logit link), not OLS, for the same reason as Figure 5: relative ECS is
# a bounded proportion. A linear term within a band is a reasonable local
# approximation even though the global relationship is curved, because
# each band spans a much narrower range of x than the full dataset (the
# logic behind piecewise regression).
#
# Reporting scale: the model is fitted on the logit scale, but a raw
# coefficient is a log-odds value, which is not readable here. Each
# band's effect is therefore reported as the predicted change in
# connectivity (percentage points, response scale) between that band's
# own 25th and 75th percentile of patch count, back-transformed with
# predict(..., type = "response").
#
# The confidence interval on that difference cannot use the coefficient's
# own standard error, because the probability difference is a nonlinear
# function of both the intercept and the slope. Instead, coefficient
# vectors are simulated from their fitted sampling distribution
# (MVN(coef(f), vcov(f))), the predicted difference is computed for each
# draw, and the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles are taken (the approach
# recommended in the mgcv documentation). MASS::mvrnorm is called via `::`
# rather than library(MASS), to avoid attaching a package that masks
# dplyr::select.
mk_bands <- function(pct_col, label, n_sim = 2000) {
  s <- sl |> filter(!is.na(.data[[pct_col]]), !is.na(n_patches), n_patches > 0)
  s$logc <- log(s$n_patches)
  br <- 10^seq(log10(min(s$total_area_ha)), log10(max(s$total_area_ha)), length.out = 9)
  s$bin <- cut(s$total_area_ha, breaks = br, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
  s |>
    group_by(bin) |>
    filter(n() >= 15) |>
    group_modify(~ {
      f <- gam(reformulate("logc", response = pct_col), data = .x, family = betar(link = "logit"))
      q <- quantile(.x$logc, c(0.25, 0.75), names = FALSE)

      pred_pt <- predict(f, newdata = data.frame(logc = q), type = "response")
      effect_pt <- 100 * (pred_pt[2] - pred_pt[1])

      Xp <- predict(f, newdata = data.frame(logc = q), type = "lpmatrix")
      draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(n_sim, mu = coef(f), Sigma = vcov(f))
      pr <- plogis(draws %*% t(Xp))
      eff_draws <- 100 * (pr[, 2] - pr[, 1])
      ci <- quantile(eff_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))

      data.frame(n = nrow(.x), amin = min(.x$total_area_ha), amax = max(.x$total_area_ha),
                 q25_patches = round(exp(q[1])), q75_patches = round(exp(q[2])),
                 slope = effect_pt, lo = unname(ci[1]), hi = unname(ci[2]))
    }) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(threshold = label, band = sprintf("%.0f–%.0f ha", amin, amax))
}

# Uses n_patches rather than nClusters_*, for the same reason as in
# Figure 5 and the matched-pairs analysis above. n_patches does not
# depend on the movement threshold, so mk_bands() needs no
# predictor-column argument; only the outcome column varies by threshold.
set.seed(20261022)  # fixed so the band confidence intervals reproduce exactly
bands <- bind_rows(
  mk_bands("ECS_pct_59", "59 m"),
  mk_bands("ECS_pct_99", "99 m")
)
bands$band <- factor(bands$band, levels = unique(bands$band[order(bands$amin)]))

fig3 <- ggplot(bands, aes(x = band, y = slope, colour = threshold)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.45), linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("59 m" = "firebrick", "99 m" = "steelblue"), name = "Dispersal\nthreshold") +
  labs(
    x = "Woodland amount band (total woodland area)",
    y = "Change in connectivity, 25th–75th pct. of patch count\n(percentage points; more negative = fragmentation hurts more)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
print(fig3)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "Fig07_effect_across_city_size.png"), fig3, width = 10, height = 6.2, dpi = 300)
write.csv(bands, file.path(figures_dir, "Supp_woodland_amount_band_effects.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Figure 7 and Supplementary Table 3: does patch spacing add anything?

Uses the same code as the `sloss_spacing_partial_effect`,
`sloss_spacing_partial_plot` and `sloss_spacing_table` chunks in
`03_National_ECS.Rmd`. The spacing measurements are read from the saved
national patch-spacing file and are not re-extracted here.

```{r results_fig7_spacing_model}
prior_spacing <- read.csv(file.path(checkpoint_dir, "08_national_patch_spacing.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

sls <- sl |>
  inner_join(prior_spacing, by = "region") |>
  filter(!is.na(median_euclidean_dist), median_euclidean_dist > 0)
cat("Regions with spacing data:", nrow(sls), "of", nrow(sl), "\n")

m_area_patches_sub <- gam(ECS_pct_59 ~ s(log_area, k = 5) + s(log(n_patches), k = 5),
                           data = sls, family = betar(link = "logit"), method = "REML")
m_spacing <- gam(ECS_pct_59 ~ s(log_area, k = 5) + s(log(n_patches), k = 5) +
                    s(log(median_euclidean_dist), k = 5),
                  data = sls, family = betar(link = "logit"), method = "REML")

cat("Deviance explained, area + patches:", round(summary(m_area_patches_sub)$dev.expl, 3), "\n")
cat("Deviance explained, + spacing:", round(summary(m_spacing)$dev.expl, 3), "\n")
cat("AIC, area + patches:", round(AIC(m_area_patches_sub), 1), "\n")
cat("AIC, + spacing:", round(AIC(m_spacing), 1), "\n")

# Does spacing explain Milton Keynes specifically, or just add general
# explanatory power? Its residual under each model answers this: if
# spacing were the missing piece for Milton Keynes, its residual would
# shrink substantially once spacing is added.
mk_idx <- which(sls$region == "Milton Keynes")
if (length(mk_idx) == 1) {
  cat("\nMilton Keynes: n_patches =", sls$n_patches[mk_idx],
      ", median inter-patch distance =", round(sls$median_euclidean_dist[mk_idx], 1), "m\n")
  cat("Milton Keynes residual, area + patches model:",
      round(residuals(m_area_patches_sub, type = "response")[mk_idx], 3), "\n")
  cat("Milton Keynes residual, + spacing model:",
      round(residuals(m_spacing, type = "response")[mk_idx], 3), "\n")
}
```

Plots the partial effect of patch spacing on relative ECS.

```{r results_fig7_spacing_partial_plot}
med_area_s <- median(sls$total_area_ha)
med_patches_s <- median(sls$n_patches)
band_s <- sls |> filter(total_area_ha >= med_area_s * 0.8, total_area_ha <= med_area_s * 1.25,
                         n_patches >= med_patches_s * 0.8, n_patches <= med_patches_s * 1.25)
spacing_min <- min(band_s$median_euclidean_dist)
spacing_max <- max(band_s$median_euclidean_dist)
cat("Regions in area+patches joint band:", nrow(band_s), "\n")
cat("Supported spacing range in that band:", round(spacing_min, 1), "-", round(spacing_max, 1), "m\n")

spacing_seq <- exp(seq(log(spacing_min), log(spacing_max), length.out = 200))
pred_grid_s <- data.frame(log_area = log(med_area_s), n_patches = med_patches_s,
                           median_euclidean_dist = spacing_seq)
pred_s <- predict(m_spacing, newdata = pred_grid_s, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
pred_df_s <- data.frame(
  spacing = spacing_seq,
  fit = plogis(pred_s$fit),
  lo = plogis(pred_s$fit - 1.96 * pred_s$se.fit),
  hi = plogis(pred_s$fit + 1.96 * pred_s$se.fit)
)

mk_spacing <- sls$median_euclidean_dist[sls$region == "Milton Keynes"]

fig_spacing_partial <- ggplot(pred_df_s, aes(x = spacing, y = fit)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(colour = "forestgreen", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mk_spacing, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = mk_spacing, y = max(pred_df_s$hi), label = "Milton Keynes\n(82m)",
           colour = "firebrick", size = 3.2, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, max(pred_df_s$hi) * 1.15)) +
  labs(
    x = "Median inter-patch distance (m, log scale)",
    y = "Predicted relative Expected Cluster Size"
  ) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, lineheight = 1.2))
print(fig_spacing_partial)
save_fig(fig_spacing_partial, "Fig_SLOSS_spacing_partial_effect", width = 9.5, height = 6.8)
```

Writes Supplementary Table 3: the regions with the most patches, with observed and predicted relative ECS.

sls$residual_pp <- 100 * (sls$ECS_pct_59 - sls$predicted_ECS_pct)

top_patches_table <- sls |>
  arrange(desc(n_patches)) |>
  slice_head(n = 12) |>
  transmute(
    Region = region,
    `Woodland (ha)` = round(total_area_ha, 1),
    Patches = n_patches,
    `Spacing (m)` = round(median_euclidean_dist, 1),
    `Actual ECS (%)` = round(100 * ECS_pct_59, 1),

print(top_patches_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(top_patches_table, file.path(figures_dir, "TableS_spacing_top_patch_count_regions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Resistance surface maps: Milton Keynes and Gloucester (Methods illustration)

Milton Keynes and Gloucester, drawn from the same surface used in the
connectivity analysis (LCM 10 m with NFI woodland added, clipped to the
region boundary). Colours come from an explicit class table, as in the
`gloucester_full_landcover` chunk of `03_National_ECS.Rmd`. Each legend
entry shows the resistance value in brackets. No title is drawn on the
image.

```{r results_resistance_surface_maps}
library(terra)

lcm_class_labels <- c(
  `1` = "Woodland",
  `3` = "Arable", `4` = "Improved grassland", `5` = "Neutral grassland",
  `6` = "Calcareous grassland", `7` = "Acid grassland",
  `8` = "Fen, marsh, swamp", `9` = "Heather", `10` = "Heather grassland",
  `11` = "Bog", `12` = "Inland rock", `13` = "Saltwater",
  `14` = "Freshwater", `15` = "Supra-littoral rock",
  `16` = "Supra-littoral sediment", `17` = "Littoral rock",
  `18` = "Littoral sediment", `19` = "Saltmarsh", `20` = "Urban",
  `21` = "Suburban"
)
resistance_plot_colours <- c(
  `1`  = "#1b5e20", `3`  = "#e8a33d", `4`  = "#7cb342", `5`  = "#e0c14c",
  `6`  = "#d4b83c", `7`  = "#c9a227", `8`  = "#8d6e52", `9`  = "#9575cd",
  `10` = "#b39ddb", `11` = "#6d4c35", `12` = "#b0a89a", `13` = "#2a9d8f",
  `14` = "#4a90d9", `15` = "#c2b8a3", `16` = "#cabb9c", `17` = "#a89f91",
  `18` = "#d1c3a3", `19` = "#c98fb0", `20` = "#4d4d4d", `21` = "#8c8c8c"
)

save_resistance_map <- function(region_name, file_name, width_px = 2800) {
  region <- urban_regions_named |> filter(bua_name == region_name)
  bbox <- st_bbox(region)
  lcm_zoom <- rast(lcm_file) |> crop(vect(st_as_sfc(bbox)))
  nfi_zoom <- st_crop(nfi_urban, bbox) |> st_collection_extract("POLYGON")
  nfi_raster <- rasterize(vect(nfi_zoom), lcm_zoom[[1]], field = 1, background = 0)

  classified <- lcm_zoom[[1]]
  classified[(lcm_zoom[[1]] %in% c(1, 2)) | (nfi_raster > 0)] <- 1
  classified <- mask(classified, vect(region)) |> trim()

  present <- sort(unique(values(classified, na.rm = TRUE)))
  present_chr <- as.character(present)
  # Class names and colours are attached to the raster by class number
  # (levels + coltab), so a colour can never slip onto the wrong class.
  levels(classified) <- data.frame(
    id = present,
    category = paste0(lcm_class_labels[present_chr], " (", resistance_lookup[present_chr], ")")
  )
  coltab(classified) <- data.frame(value = present, col = unname(resistance_plot_colours[present_chr]))

  woodland_ha <- sum(values(classified) == 1, na.rm = TRUE) * prod(res(classified)) / 10000
  cat(region_name, "woodland on this map:", round(woodland_ha, 1), "ha\n")

  height_px <- round(width_px * nrow(classified) / ncol(classified)) + 100
  png(file.path(figures_dir, file_name), width = width_px, height = height_px, res = 300)
  plot(classified, axes = FALSE, mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5),
       plg = list(x = "topright", cex = 0.9, title = "Surface type (resistance)"))
  dev.off()
  invisible(file.path(figures_dir, file_name))
}

save_resistance_map("Milton Keynes", "Fig_resistance_surface_milton_keynes.png")
save_resistance_map("Gloucester", "Fig_resistance_surface_gloucester.png")
```

Alternative version: the same two surfaces coloured by resistance value
(1 = woodland, 10 = hardest to cross) on one shared colour bar, side by
side.

```{r results_resistance_surface_pair}
library(terra)

resistance_value_raster <- function(region_name) {
  region <- urban_regions_named |> filter(bua_name == region_name)
  bbox <- st_bbox(region)
  lcm_zoom <- rast(lcm_file) |> crop(vect(st_as_sfc(bbox)))
  nfi_zoom <- st_crop(nfi_urban, bbox) |> st_collection_extract("POLYGON")
  nfi_raster <- rasterize(vect(nfi_zoom), lcm_zoom[[1]], field = 1, background = 0)

  classified <- lcm_zoom[[1]]
  classified[(lcm_zoom[[1]] %in% c(1, 2)) | (nfi_raster > 0)] <- 1
  classified <- mask(classified, vect(region)) |> trim()

  resistance_r <- subst(classified, from = as.numeric(names(resistance_lookup)), to = as.numeric(resistance_lookup))
  # A cell with no land-cover class stays 0 after the lookup; treat it as blank.
  ifel(resistance_r == 0, NA, resistance_r)
}

# Resistance 1 (woodland) = dark green, resistance 10 = white.
resistance_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("#00441b", "#238b45", "#74c476", "#c7e9c0", "#ffffff"))(100)

# Highlighted version: each resistance value that occurs in these two cities
# gets its own step, lightening from deep green (woodland) to a soft cream
# (resistance 10), so 8 and 10 can be told apart without a glaring white.
resistance_steps <- c(`1` = "#00441b", `2` = "#5cb765", `5` = "#8fcf8a", `6` = "#a8d9a0",
                      `7` = "#c0e1b6", `8` = "#d9edc9", `10` = "#f4f1e6")
woodland_green <- "#00441b"

r_mk <- resistance_value_raster("Milton Keynes")
r_gl <- resistance_value_raster("Gloucester")

# Every resistance value in the two maps needs a colour step.
stopifnot(all(unique(c(values(r_mk), values(r_gl))[!is.na(c(values(r_mk), values(r_gl)))]) %in%
                as.numeric(names(resistance_steps))))

draw_resistance_panel <- function(r, city_label, region_name, scale_km, sbar_pos = "bottomleft",
                                  highlight_woodland = FALSE) {
  if (!highlight_woodland) {
    plot(r, col = resistance_palette, range = c(1, 10), legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE,
         mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2.5, 0.5), main = city_label)
  } else {
    r_cat <- r
    ids <- as.numeric(names(resistance_steps))
    levels(r_cat) <- data.frame(id = ids, label = as.character(ids))
    coltab(r_cat) <- data.frame(value = ids, col = unname(resistance_steps))
    plot(r_cat, legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE, mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2.5, 0.5), main = city_label)
    woodland <- ifel(r == 1, 1, NA)
    plot(as.polygons(woodland), col = NA, border = woodland_green, lwd = 0.6, add = TRUE)
  }
  # Thin outline so the city shape stays visible.
  plot(vect(urban_regions_named |> filter(bua_name == region_name)), border = "grey40", lwd = 0.8, add = TRUE)
  sbar(scale_km * 1000, xy = sbar_pos, type = "bar", divs = 2, below = "km",
       labels = c(0, scale_km / 2, scale_km), cex = 0.9)
}

save_resistance_pair <- function(file_name, highlight_woodland) {
  total_w <- ncol(r_mk) + ncol(r_gl)
  png(file.path(figures_dir, file_name),
      width = 5400, height = round(5400 * max(nrow(r_mk), nrow(r_gl)) / (total_w * 1.06)) + 150, res = 300)
  layout(matrix(1:3, nrow = 1), widths = c(ncol(r_mk), ncol(r_gl), 0.06 * total_w))
  draw_resistance_panel(r_mk, "Milton Keynes", "Milton Keynes", 4, highlight_woodland = highlight_woodland)
  draw_resistance_panel(r_gl, "Gloucester", "Gloucester", 2, "bottomright", highlight_woodland = highlight_woodland)

  par(mar = c(8, 0.5, 4, 4.5))
  if (!highlight_woodland) {
    y <- seq(1, 10, length.out = 200)
    image(x = 1, y = y, z = matrix(y, nrow = 1),
          col = resistance_palette[pmin(100, pmax(1, round((y - 1) / 9 * 99) + 1))],
          axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
    axis(4, at = 1:10, las = 1, cex.axis = 1.1)
  } else {
    n_steps <- length(resistance_steps)
    image(x = 1, y = seq_len(n_steps), z = matrix(seq_len(n_steps), nrow = 1),
          col = unname(resistance_steps), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
    axis(4, at = seq_len(n_steps), labels = names(resistance_steps), las = 1, cex.axis = 1.1)
  }
  mtext("Resistance (1 = woodland)", side = 4, line = 3.2, cex = 0.95)
  box()
  dev.off()
}

save_resistance_pair("Fig_resistance_surface_by_resistance_pair.png", highlight_woodland = FALSE)
save_resistance_pair("Fig_resistance_surface_by_resistance_pair_woodland_highlight.png", highlight_woodland = TRUE)
```

# Urban region delineation figure (London), illustrating the morphological closing (Methods illustration)

Draws the delineation of London in three panels: the raw built-up areas, after closing, and the final region.

```{r closing_stages_london}
library(sf)

plot_closing_stages <- function(
  bbox = st_bbox(
    c(xmin = 500000, ymin = 145000, xmax = 570000, ymax = 210000),
    crs = st_crs(27700)
  ),
  region_name = "London",
  out_file = file.path(figures_dir, "supp_closing_stages_london.png")
) {

  urban_closed <- readRDS(file.path(checkpoint_dir, "05_urban_closed.rds"))

  # The final panel shows the delineated region alone, not a bbox crop of
  # the general hole-filled layer, which would also show other regions
  # inside the same rectangular window.
  region_final <- urban_regions_named |> filter(bua_name == region_name)

  woodland_bbox <- st_crop(nfi_urban, bbox) |> st_collection_extract("POLYGON")
  # Intersection with the polygon itself, not a bbox crop: a bbox crop is
  # a rectangle, so woodland outside London's irregular boundary but
  # inside the rectangle would still show.
  woodland_region <- suppressWarnings(st_intersection(
    st_crop(nfi_urban, st_bbox(region_final)), region_final
  )) |> st_collection_extract("POLYGON")

  xl <- bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")]; yl <- bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")]

  # Rendered to a fixed-size PNG device explicitly, because knitr's
  # fig.width and fig.height are honoured only on a full knit, not when a
  # chunk is run interactively. Panel dimensions (4 in x 3.71 in) follow
  # the bbox's aspect ratio (70 km / 65 km) so all three panels are
  # identically proportioned, and all three share the same xlim and ylim
  # rather than auto-fitting to their own extent.
  png(out_file, width = 12.3, height = 4.16, units = "in", res = 300)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mai = c(0.05, 0.05, 0.4, 0.05))

  plot(
    st_geometry(st_crop(bua, bbox)),
    col = "grey70", border = "black",
    main = paste0("Raw BUAs: ", region_name),
    xlim = xl, ylim = yl
  )
  plot(st_geometry(woodland_bbox), col = "darkgreen", border = NA, add = TRUE)
  # Highlights a cluster of gaps between raw BUAs that closing later
  # fills (the circle coordinates are hard-coded).
  symbols(520130, 173274, circles = 4530, inches = FALSE, add = TRUE, fg = "red", lwd = 3)

  plot(
    st_geometry(st_crop(urban_closed, bbox)),
    col = "grey70", border = "black",
    main = paste0("After closing: ", region_name),
    xlim = xl, ylim = yl
  )
  plot(st_geometry(woodland_bbox), col = "darkgreen", border = NA, add = TRUE)

  plot(
    st_geometry(region_final),
    col = "grey70", border = "black",
    main = paste0("After hole-fill: ", region_name),
    xlim = xl, ylim = yl
  )
  plot(st_geometry(woodland_region), col = "darkgreen", border = NA, add = TRUE)

  dev.off()
  knitr::include_graphics(out_file)
}

plot_closing_stages()
```
